newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins edge down, shrug off reshuffle.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins edge down, shrug off reshuffle.

text.p: MinFin bonds edged down, following the general downward trend of the emerging markets, despite Monday's government appointments of reformers which were already priced in, dealers said.
Itar-Tass news agency said on Monday reformist Anatoly Chubais will be Finance Minister as well as First Deputy Prime Minister in the new Russian cabinet.
President Boris Yeltsin appointed Boris Nemtsov, governor of Nizhny Novgorod who is famous for his reforms, first deputy prime minister alongside Chubais on Monday.

"Prices eased earlier on foreign selling as the general (emerging market) trend is down. The day is otherwise quiet," an International Moscow Bank dealer said and added the new government's outline could revive the market.
Earlier the Kremlin said President Boris Yeltsin would announce later on Monday the membership and structure of the new cabinet.
Another dealer said the market had alreday priced in the strengthening role of Chubais last week.
"People already have the paper they wanted and it seems they do need to buy more today," he said.
Dealers said the fourth, fifth and sixth tranches were traded the most actively.
